panels.title: Controller version
panels.description: Version label from wvc_build_info gauge. If this ever shows two versions, a rolling deploy is in-flight or an old worker didn't restart.

panels.title: Nodes online
panels.description: Count of nodes with status='online'. Amber < full complement, red = fewer than 3.

panels.title: VMs running
panels.description: Total VMs currently reporting state=running.

panels.title: VMs total
panels.description: All VMs known to the controller (any state).

panels.title: Cluster RAM used %
panels.description: Sum of available RAM across online nodes vs total. Aggregated at scrape time — the nodes report the truth as libvirt sees it.

panels.title: Cluster vCPUs (total)
panels.description: Sum of total physical vCPUs across online nodes. NOTE: `wvc_cluster_vcpus_available` currently equals total (nodes don't decrement free vCPU on VM allocation — libvirt oversubscription model), so a 'used %' panel would be meaningless here. RAM is the real capacity constraint.

panels.title: VMs by state
panels.description: Distribution of VMs by libvirt state at scrape time.

panels.title: VMs by state over time
panels.description: Stacked view of VMs-by-state; watch for spikes in `crashed` or sudden movement between `running` and `stopped`.

panels.title: Nodes by status
panels.description: Node status breakdown — normally all online. `offline` appearing means node_monitor's SSH poll is failing.

panels.title: Cluster RAM (MB)
panels.description: Cluster RAM total (physical) vs available (free per libvirt). Gap = allocated to running VMs. NOTE: the base-1024 unit converts MB→GiB display auto, which is close enough for a capacity dashboard.

panels.title: HTTP request rate by status class
panels.description: Rolling 5-minute request rate, stacked by HTTP status class. A healthy controller is ~all 2xx with a low background of 4xx (auth challenges, 404s).

panels.title: HTTP request latency percentiles
panels.description: Global HTTP latency percentiles across all endpoints. p99 sustained > 1s is worth investigating; migrate/create endpoints will legitimately push p99 up.

panels.title: Top 10 slowest endpoints (p95, last 5m)
panels.description: Ten slowest Flask endpoints by 5-minute p95 latency. Endpoints like `vms.migrate_vm` legitimately dominate; a sudden `vms.list_vms` climb usually indicates DB lag.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx error rate
panels.description: Per-endpoint 5xx rate. Should be flat zero. Any sustained non-zero line here is an alert-worthy regression.

panels.title: VM operation rate by operation
panels.description: Rate of admin-initiated VM operations (create.*, power.*, edit, delete, migrate) grouped by op. Not stacked by result — that's the next panel.

panels.title: VM migration duration percentiles
panels.description: Migration duration percentiles by mode (live vs offline). Only successful migrations are observed — a failure that returned in 0.1s (CPU mismatch refusal) is not in this histogram.

panels.title: vm_sync iteration duration
panels.description: How long each vm_sync loop iteration takes across all online nodes. p95 > 5s means one of the nodes is slow to SSH. The 'errors/s' series has different units but overlaying it here saves a panel; watch for any non-zero.

panels.title: node_poll duration by result
panels.description: Per-node SSH poll duration p95 (ok vs fail buckets separated) and a fail-rate overlay. Sustained non-zero fail rate means SSH into a node is broken; check node_monitor logs.

panels.title: LDAP bind rate
panels.description: LDAP bind rate broken down by kind (service|user|group_query) and result (ok|fail). A sudden spike of user/fail = someone brute-forcing or an AD outage.

panels.title: LDAP bind failure ratio (5m)
panels.description: Fraction of LDAP binds that failed, per kind. `service` failing = the controller can't talk to AD at all; `user` failing spike = brute-force or wrong password rollout; `group_query` failing = AD ACL / OU permissions changed. The clamp_min prevents 0/0 spikes when no binds are happening.

targets.expr: sum by (kind) (rate(wvc_ldap_binds_total{result="fail"}[5m])) / ignoring(result) group_left clamp_min(sum by (kind) (rate(wvc_ldap_binds_total[5m])), 0.001)

panels.title: VMs created (total, all time)
panels.description: Count of rows in the vms table. Includes currently-active VMs; deleted VMs are removed from this table.

panels.title: VMs created per day (last 90 days)
panels.description: Count of new rows in vms grouped by day (created_at). Deleted VMs no longer appear.

targets.rawSql: SELECT DATE(created_at) AS time, COUNT(*) AS 'VMs created' FROM vms WHERE created_at >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) GROUP BY DATE(created_at) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Login attempts per minute by result
panels.description: rate(wvc_logins_total[5m]) split by result (success | invalid_credentials | missing_fields). Sudden spike in invalid_credentials could indicate credential-stuffing.

panels.title: Successful logins (last 24h)
panels.description: sum(increase(wvc_logins_total{result="success"}[24h]))

panels.title: Failed logins (last 24h)
panels.description: sum(increase(wvc_logins_total{result!="success"}[24h]))

panels.title: Total logins (all time)
panels.description: Successful logins counted by the api Prometheus counter. Resets on api pod restart.

panels.title: VMs created (all time)
panels.description: Process-lifetime counter for create.blank / create.clone / create.existing / create.quick with result=ok. Resets on api pod restart — see also DB-sourced panel above for durable count.

panels.title: VMs created (time range)
panels.description: Count of successful VM create operations over the selected time range. Change the time picker (top-right) to switch between day / week / month / etc.

panels.title: VMs deleted (time range)
panels.description: Count of successful VM deletes over the selected time range.

panels.title: Logins (time range)
panels.description: Successful logins over the selected time range.

panels.title: VM actions rate (start / stop / edit / console)
panels.description: Actions per minute at the selected resolution. 'console open' counts successful POSTs to /api/vms/<id>/console.

panels.title: VM actions total over range (choose day/week/month via time picker)
panels.description: Single value per series = cumulative count over the selected range.
